statement: A court may infer that possession, initially that of a co-owner, has subsequently become adverse against other co-owners, based on the lapse of time and the circumstances of the case.
supporting_quote: If it is found that one co-owner and his predecessors in interest have been in possession of the whole property for a period as far back as reasonable memory reaches; that he and they have done nothing to recognize the claims of the other co-owners; that he and they have taken the whole produce of the property for themselves; and that these co-owners have never done anything to assert a claim to any share of the produce, it is artificial in the highest degree to say that such a person and his predecessors in interest must be presumed to be possessing all this time in the capacity of co-owners, and that they can never be regarded as having possessed adversely, simply because no definite positive act can be pointed to as originating or demonstrating the adverse possession.

statement: The progress of prescription is not arrested by the minority of the plaintiffs or the absence of their father beyond the seas.
supporting_quote: the mere fact that his succession passed to the plaintiffs on his death, and that they were minors at the time, cannot arrest the progress of prescription.

statement: An interim injunction should not be refused solely on the basis that damages are quantifiable.
supporting_quote: For these reasons, an interim injunction should not be refused solely on the basis that damages are quantifiable.

statement: A partition decree cannot be the subject of a private arrangement between parties on matters of title which the Court is bound by law to examine.
supporting_quote: While it is indeed essential for parties to a partition action to state to the Court the points of contest inter se and to obtain a determination on them, the obligations of the Court are not discharged unless the provisions of section 25 of the Act are complied with quite independently of what parties may or may not do.

statement: A court exercising revisionary jurisdiction can correct errors, including those that violate statutory provisions, even if the affected party has failed to appeal.
supporting_quote: Disregarding a statutory provision alone would amount to have established exceptional circumstances that are necessary to invoke revisionary jurisdiction.

statement: A person who seeks a declaration of title to the property in suit must prove his title.
supporting_quote: A person who seeks a declaration of title to the property in suit must prove his title. This view is supported by the following judicial decisions.

statement: A District Judge presiding over a partition action should not wait for some lapse on the part of the plaintiff to dismiss the action and relieve himself of further responsibility.
supporting_quote: A District Judge presiding over a partition action should not wait for some lapse on the part of the plaintiff to dismiss the action and relieve himself of further responsibility.

statement: A bona fide purchaser cannot be held not to own the property he bought on the ground that his predecessor was holding the property under a constructive trust, specially when the person on behalf of whom he was holding the property in trust, directs him to transfer the same to another.
supporting_quote: A bona fide purchaser cannot be held not to own the property he bought on the ground that his predecessor was holding the property under a constructive trust, specially when the person on behalf of whom he was holding the property in trust, directs him to transfer the same to another.

statement: A mortgagee is entitled to restrain the mortgagor from conduct which would prejudice the mortgage security.
supporting_quote: Halsbury’s Laws of England , Volume 32 (4th Edition) at paragraph 596 on page 286 states that “the Mortgagee is entitled to restrain the mortgagor from conduct which would prejudice the mortgage security.”

statement: Substitution in appellate proceedings does not confer upon the person substituted the status of a legal heir of the deceased party.
supporting_quote: It is therefore not necessary to substitute all heirs of the deceased as parties to the appeal. As I have already stated, substitution is solely for the limited purpose of prosecuting the appeal.

statement: A notary's failure to comply with Section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance does not vitiate mortgage documents.
supporting_quote: Thus, we find this argument based on non-compliance with the rules set out in the Notaries Ordinance would not hold water.

statement: A party is not precluded from leading evidence aliunde to controvert the consideration stated in a deed.
supporting_quote: By reason of proviso (1) to Section 92 of the Evidence Ordinance, a party is not per se precluded from leading evidence aliunde to controvert the consideration stated in a deed.

statement: Claims arising out of goods sold and delivered become prescribed in 1 year.
supporting_quote: As observed by the learned Judge of the High Court, in terms of section 8 of the Prescription Ordinance, claims arising out of such transactions become prescribed in 1 year.

statement: A company's managing director cannot be faulted for failing to make entries in the fixed asset register when the company has a Board of Directors.
supporting_quote: In any event, the Managing Director alone cannot be faulted for failing to make entries in the fixed asset register when the company has a Board of Directors, of which the Plaintiff is only one member.

statement: A contract for the sale of goods requires a sale and delivery of the goods within a year for the prescriptive period to apply.
supporting_quote: No action shall be maintainable for or in respect of any goods sold and delivered, or for any shop bill or book debt, or for work and labour done, or for the wages of artisans, laborers, or servants, unless the same shall be brought within one year after the debt shall have become due.

statement: The prescription period for an action without a written agreement is three years from the date of the cause of action.
supporting_quote: In the case of an unwritten agreement, an action should be filed within three years from the breach of the said agreement (from the date of the cause of action), in terms of section 7 of the said Ordinance.

statement: A surety who has undertaken liability as co-principal debtor has impliedly and tacitly renounced their right to plead the defence of beneficium ordinis seu excussionis.
supporting_quote: I am therefore of the view that by undertaking liability as co-principal debtor, the Defendants have impliedly as well as tacitly renounced their right to plead the defence of beneficium ordinis seu excussionis.

statement: A written contract can be constituted by an acknowledgement of liability to pay a sum due for goods bought on credit followed by a statement.
supporting_quote: an acknowledgement of liability to pay a sum due for goods bought on credit followed by a statement

statement: The burden of proof is on the judgment debtor to establish substantial losses if the writ is issued.
supporting_quote: In the light of the foregoing case law this Court finds that the burden of proof is on the Petitioner (judgement – debtor) to establish substantial losses if the writ is issued.

statement: The undertaking of the Secretary to the Treasury contained in clauses 9 and 10 of the Agreement binds the State.
supporting_quote: The undertaking of the Secretary to the Treasury contained in clauses 9 and 10 of the Agreement marked P7, binds the State.

statement: An action based on a written contract is not prescribed if brought within six years from the date of the breach of such contract.
supporting_quote: Section 6 of the Prescription Ordinance provides that; “No action shall be maintainable upon ... any written promise, contract, bargain, or agreement, ... unless such action shall be brought within six years from the date of the breach of such ... contract, bargain or agreement, ... from the date when such note or bill shall have become due, or of the last payment of interest thereon.”

statement: A company's name change does not imply a formation of a new corporate entity or a dissolution of the old company, and it still recognizes the continued existence of the old company and rights and obligations attached to it.
supporting_quote: Nevertheless, the effect of changing the name does not imply a formation of a new corporate entity or a dissolution of old company. Consequently, when a company changes its name, it still recognizes the continued existence of the old company and rights and obligations attached to it notwithstanding the change of the name.

statement: A demand for repayment of a loan repayable on demand will arise only at the time when a demand is made.
supporting_quote: It is settled law that the cause of action concerning a loan repayable on demand will arise only at the time when a demand is made [Seylan Bank Ltd v. Inter Trade Garments (Pvt.) Ltd. (2005) 1 Sri.L.R 80; Sivasubramaniam v. Alagamutui (1950) 53 N.L.R 150; See also, Bank of Ceylon v. Flex Port (Pvt.) Ltd., SC Appeal 120/2012, S.C.M. 03.07.2020 at pages 6-7].

statement: Damages must be confined to the loss suffered and maintain a balance between the seriousness of the infringement and the remedy ordered.
supporting_quote: Damages under section 170 must be “adequate to compensate ... for the loss suffered” and must maintain a balance between the seriousness of the infringement and the remedy ordered.

statement: A defendant who fails to move the court to try an issue as a preliminary issue at the commencement of the trial is deemed to have waived objections in regard to lack of jurisdiction of the court to hear and determine the defendant's action.
supporting_quote: His failure to move Court to try the said issue as a preliminary issue on such a vital matter will amount to a waiver of objections in regard to lack of jurisdiction of Court to hear and determine the defendant’s action.
